title: What to ship
description:
Decide which runtime files must ship with a program from its imports.

```
game.exe imports: VCRUNTIME140.dll, MSVCP140.dll, api-ms-win-crt-runtime-l1-1-0.dll, KERNEL32.dll, d3d11.dll
ship: the Visual C++ Redistributable (x64)
already on Windows: KERNEL32.dll, d3d11.dll
API sets (part of Windows 10+): api-ms-win-crt-runtime-l1-1-0.dll
debug runtime found: no
```
hints: After lower-casing, a name that begins with `api-ms-` is an API set (lesson 1.06): `name.compare(0, 7, "api-ms-") == 0` tests how a string begins (C++20 also has `name.starts_with("api-ms-")`). For the debug runtime, look at the end instead: `name.size() >= 5 && name.compare(name.size() - 5, 5, "d.dll") == 0` is true for a lower-cased `vcruntime140d.dll`.
Keep small sets of known names (the runtime DLLs and the system DLLs you expect), and treat anything else as "your own: ship it".
requirements: Classify each import: Visual C++ runtime, debug runtime (ends in `D.dll`, like `VCRUNTIME140D.dll`), API set, system DLL, or your own.
Compare names without caring about case.
Refuse to ship when a debug runtime is imported, with a clear message.
stretch: Print the `/MT` (static runtime) alternative and what it changes.
